$comment: Every asset this project downloads, in one place. `npm run download-assets`
reads this file and nothing else, so an asset that is not listed here is not
reproducible and should not be relied on.
NOTHING FROM A RETAIL QUAKE III INSTALL BELONGS IN THIS FILE. Commercial Q3
content is not redistributable and is not downloadable; it is sourced from the
user's own installation via tools/build-devpak.ts. See NOTICE.
`sha256` is recorded on first successful download so later runs can detect a
changed upstream. A null sha means 'not yet pinned' -- the download will
succeed and print the hash to paste back in.
An entry with `manual` cannot be fetched by a script (a JS bot challenge, a
click-through). The tool prints instructions instead of pretending otherwise,
and still runs `extract` if the file has been placed by hand.

downloads.name: openarena-pak0
downloads.description: OpenArena 0.8.8 baseoa/pak0.pk3. Third-party MD3 models and textures for the asset tests.
downloads.license: GPLv2 (OpenArena). Freely redistributable. See NOTICE.
$note: 38MB, 150 .md3 files, and player models grism/sarge/sorceress.
This is what makes test/assets/md3.test.ts run on a clean checkout: a
writer and a parser built from the same struct definitions agree with
each other even when both are wrong, so only third-party files settle
the on-disk layout.
The SourceForge /download URL redirects to a mirror with an expiring
token, so the stable /download form is what belongs here -- never the
resolved master.dl.sourceforge.net link.

downloads.name: oa-decal-burn_med_mrk
downloads.description: OpenArena gfx/damage/burn_med_mrk.tga. The scorch a rocket, grenade or plasma bolt leaves; EVERY bundled course needs it.
downloads.license: GPLv2 (OpenArena). Freely redistributable, and unlike retail Quake III content it MAY be committed. See NOTICE.
$note: The three gfx/damage marks are the one image group that is NOT about a
particular map. `decals.ts` loads them by fixed path and builds no mark
pool at all without them ('no art, no shadow', the same fallback
shadow.ts uses), so a course whose pak omits them simply never shows a
bullet hole or a rocket scorch -- silently, with nothing in the console.
That is what the bundled courses did until 2026-09-10, and it read as a
renderer bug rather than a missing file.
So they go in EVERY course kit, spread from DECAL_KIT in
tools/build-oapak.ts rather than repeated four times.
Byte-identical to the copies inside oa-pak0.pk3 above (verified by
sha256), so the SVN is the same content and not a re-encode. Fetched
individually anyway, for the same reason every other texture here is:
95KB against 38MB, and each file carries its own hash.
bullet_mrk is .jpg and the other two are .tga -- that is how OpenArena
ships them, and `findImage` resolves the extension, so the paths in the
kit must match the real files rather than being normalised.

downloads.name: dfwc2021-7
downloads.description: DFWC 2021 map 7 (kabcorp), in plain IBSP form.
downloads.license: Undocumented. A community competition map; per-file licensing is not published, which is why it is downloaded rather than committed.
downloads.manual: ws.q3df.org sits behind a Cloudflare JS challenge, which returns 403 to any scripted client. Open the URL in a browser, then save the .pk3 to the path below and re-run this command.
$note: Get this map from q3df, NOT from the copy that ships in some Quake III
installations. The competition build wraps its .bsp in an 'EZPZ'
container so only the organisers' client will open it -- the file is
intact and the .pk3 unzips fine, it simply is not a BSP. Stock Quake III
rejects it too: CM_LoadMap checks the version field and that build
reports 48 where Quake III wants 46.
`parseBsp` recognises the EZPZ ident and says so by name rather than
failing with a hex number. Unwrapping it is deliberately not
implemented: the wrapper exists to control which clients can read the
map, and the maps are published unprotected afterwards anyway.

downloads.name: font-barlow-condensed-regular
downloads.description: Barlow Condensed Regular (400). Headings and numerals in the UI design system (design/).
downloads.license: SIL Open Font License 1.1. Freely redistributable. See NOTICE.
$note: Static per-weight files, not the variable font -- Barlow Condensed's
google/fonts entry ships one TTF per weight rather than a [wght] axis
file, unlike JetBrains Mono below.
Unlike the game-content downloads in this manifest, font files ARE
committed to the repository: they are OFL-licensed (freely
redistributable, unlike retail Quake III content) and the menu shell
needs them to render correctly on a clean clone with no network access
and no player-supplied .pk3 mounted yet. `public/fonts/` is therefore
NOT gitignored, unlike the rest of public/. Re-run this command only to
refresh from upstream; the checked-in files are what ships.

downloads.description: JetBrains Mono, variable weight axis 100-800. Data, labels and paths in the UI design system (design/).
downloads.license: SIL Open Font License 1.1. Freely redistributable. See NOTICE.
$note: One file, a variable font -- `font-weight: 400 700` in the @font-face
rule lets the browser interpolate 500 rather than needing a fourth
static file. See font-barlow-condensed-regular's note on why this is
committed rather than gitignored like the rest of public/.
`dest` renames upstream's `JetBrainsMono[wght].ttf` -- square brackets
are both a glob metacharacter and Rollup's output-placeholder syntax
([name], [hash]), and `vite build` processes this file's @font-face
url() and index.html's <link> for it. There is no reason to keep
upstream's filename; `dest` is this project's to choose.

downloads.name: cpma-1.53
downloads.description: Challenge ProMode Arena 1.53, maps omitted. Read for its VM bytecode only -- see .agent/plans/CPMA-REVERSE-ENG.md.
downloads.license: PROPRIETARY. Freely downloadable from the CPMA project; NOT redistributable, and NOT GPL. Reference material in the same sense as refs/, except that unlike refs/ it is not even upstream-redistributable. Never committed, never shipped, never imported.
$note: The one entry here that is not free software, and the reason it is
allowed is narrow: CPM mode in src/physics/cpm.ts is the only part of
physics/ without a readable original to diff against, so its constants
rest on community prose. CPMA's shipped .qvm bytecode settles them.
What comes out of it is numbers -- `AIR_STOP_ACCELERATE is 2.5` -- and
never expression. No decompiled bodies, no transcribed control flow.
The plan spells out the line; read it before running the tool.
dest is under refs/, which .gitignore excludes wholesale, so a stray
`git add -A` cannot commit the archive by accident.
As of 2026-08-28 cdn.playmorepromote.com is denied by this
environment's egress policy (403 at CONNECT) on all three hostnames,
so this entry is `optional` and download-assets reports it as skipped
rather than failing the run. A mirror on an allowed host is
deliberately not substituted.
